column2: 朝扣富儿门，暮随肥马尘。残杯与冷炙，到处潜悲辛。
column3: At dawn I knock on the rich man's gate; at dusk I follow fat horses' dust. Leftover wine and cold scraps — everywhere I swallow grief unseen.

column2: 清晨去敲富豪的大门，傍晚随在达官贵人的马后吃尘土；吃的是别人的残羹冷炙，到处偷偷吞咽着悲伤与痛苦。即使如此的下贱，但仍然吃不上饭。
column3: Knocking on wealthy doors at dawn, eating dust behind nobles' horses at dusk; surviving on others' leftovers, secretly swallowing sorrow and bitterness wherever you go. Even debasing yourself this way, you still can't get enough to eat.

column2: 去【坊市】行动出卖体力之后去【出游】可以有效获取生命。
column3: After working at the [Market Ward] to sell your labor, going on an [Excursion] is an effective way to regain health.

column2: 昔年泰山清狂，不知薪米之贵；今入长安，方知出卖体力之迫切也。
column3: In years past atop Mount Tai, carefree and wild, I never knew the cost of firewood and rice. Now entering Chang'an, I finally understand the urgency of selling one's labor.

column2: 去坊市出卖体力之后去出游可以有效获取额外的资源。
column3: Working at the Market Ward to sell your labor, then going on an Excursion, is an effective way to gain extra resources.

column2: 昔年泰山清狂，不知薪米之贵；今入长安，方知出卖体力之迫切也。
column3: In years past atop Mount Tai, carefree and wild, I never knew the cost of firewood and rice. Now entering Chang'an, I finally understand the urgency of selling one's labor.

column2: 疟疠三秋孰可忍，寒热百日相交战
column3: How can one endure three autumns of pestilence and plague? A hundred days of cold and fever clashing within.

column2: 体内的寒气与热毒像两支军队一样，在我的身体里交锋厮杀。
column3: Cold qi and heat toxin battle inside my body like two armies at war.

column2: …或许和西市地下神医打好关系到【相识】之后他有办法？
column3: ...Perhaps the underground divine doctor of the West Market has a remedy once you've earned his [Acquaintance]?

column2: 莫硬撑了！那寒热消渴非小疾，快去求医。莫等老来右臂偏枯、日夕枯渴，徒留一身病骨，悔之晚矣！
column3: Don't tough it out! That alternation of cold, fever, and wasting thirst is no minor ailment — go seek a doctor at once! Don't wait until old age, when your right arm withers and day and night you parch with thirst, leaving only a body of bone and sickness — by then it will be too late for regret!

column2: 你终于拿到了对应的官职，你唯一想做的事情就是回家报喜，改善家人的生活。
column3: You've finally secured an official post. The only thing you want to do now is rush home with the good news and improve your family's life.
Leaving the City at Year's End
You decide to exchange a poem with {@target_npc}
Accept the silver and thank the fellow villager

column2:
同乡老张风尘仆仆地找到你，从怀里掏出一个灰布包裹塞进你手中。

「这是三十钱，乡里凑的。子美啊，你到长安也有些时日了，怎么还不去拜谒？这都第三旬了，再不去可就晚了！」

他说完，重重拍了拍你的肩，转身消失在街巷尽头。

（天意旁白：是时候了，点击右下角「拜谒」行动，叩响仕途的第一扇门。）
column3:
Your fellow villager Old Zhang finds you, travel-worn and dusty. He pulls a grey cloth bundle from his coat and presses it into your hands.

"Here's thirty coins, scraped together by the village. Zimei, you've been in Chang'an for some time now — why haven't you gone to pay your respects yet? It's already the third xun! Much longer and it'll be too late!"

He gives your shoulder a heavy pat, then turns and vanishes into the alley.

(Aside from Providence: The time has come. Tap the "Pay Respects" action in the lower right, and knock on the first door of officialdom.)

column2: 寒月孤雪落叶：羁旅登高，天地苍茫
column3: Cold Moon, Lonely Snow, Falling Leaves: Climbing high on a distant journey, heaven and earth vast and boundless

column2: 你展开卷轴，墨迹未干。这是一首平平无奇的诗，自我安慰尚可，赠人则略显寒酸。
column3: You unroll the scroll; the ink is still damp. This is a thoroughly unremarkable poem — passable for self-consolation, but rather shabby as a gift.

column2: 你展开卷轴，墨迹未干。这是一首颇有章法的诗，令人点头称赞，唯欠几分神来之笔。
column3: You unroll the scroll; the ink is still damp. This poem has genuine craft — it earns nods of approval, lacking only that touch of divine inspiration.

column2: 你展开卷轴，墨迹未干。这是一首泣鬼惊神的绝唱！字字珠玑，力透纸背，必将千古流传。
column3: You unroll the scroll; the ink is still damp. This is a masterpiece that moves ghosts and gods to tears! Each word a pearl, the brushwork biting through the page — this will be passed down through the ages.

column2: 你展开卷轴，墨迹未干。一首「{@poem_type}」诗已然落成。
column3: You unroll the scroll; the ink is still damp. A poem of "{@poem_type}" has taken form.

column2: 干将未省钝 + 主将收才子：献赋求荐，含蓄自尊
column3: Ganjiang unaware of his own dullness + the Commander gathers talents: offering verse to seek recommendation, restrained yet proud

column2: 赠献纳使起居田舍人澄
column3: For the Palace Provisioner, Drafter Tian of Qiju

column2: 求职诗的巅峰：骑驴十三载(羁旅) + 骅骝作骨(骐骥) + 致君尧舜上(尧舜)
column3: The pinnacle of job-seeking poetry: thirteen years on donkey-back (Wandering) + a steed's spirit in the bones (Noble Steed) + raising the sovereign to the level of Yao and Shun (Sages)

column2: 奉赠韦左丞丈二十二韵
column3: Twenty-Two Couplets Humbly Presented to Vice Director Wei

column2: 饥寒 + 明主：谏议底色，穷年忧黎
column3: Hunger, Cold + A Wise Ruler: the remonstrator's essence — year after year of poverty, grieving for the common people
Ten Couplets Respectfully Presented to Remonstrator Zheng

column2: 才名与望誉。行卷投谒、风评交游的核心资本，是进入权贵圈层的入场券。
column3: Reputation and renown. The core capital for submitting manuscripts, paying visits, and navigating social circles — your ticket into the world of the powerful.
Literary talent stirs; a faint name begins to rise.

column2: 才名渐起，坊间偶有传颂
column3: Your reputation grows; your name is occasionally praised in the streets.

column2: 声名鹊起，文人争相传颂
column3: Your fame soars; scholars compete to recite your works.
The literary star stirs; all under heaven knows your name.
Your literary name is slightly tarnished.
Your literary name is damaged, drawing considerable criticism.
Your name is in ruins; everyone spits at the mention of it.
A name that moves the world
Tossed on the sea of officialdom
A fledgling on the official path
